correctness.rationale: With generator d²/dx² the reflected kernels have direct and image terms (4πt)^−1/2 exp(−(x∓y)²/(4t)). The squared commutator norm integrates twice over E×E^c, and row-square bounds give finiteness for every finite-measure E. Subtracting the signed kernel squares gives the product of the two complementary Gaussian masses with prefactor 2/(πt), exactly q(1−q), with equality at q=1/2. Dilation followed by integration of Q from 0 to 2c gives the common interval term and the cross term factors. For the Dirichlet derivative, multiplying by πexp(c²/2) gives H as in the original; H(0)=0 and H′>0. The analogous Neumann G goes from 2sqrt(π/2) to −sqrt(π/2); Q(2c)<exp(−2c²)/(2c) makes G′ strictly negative, proving the unique peak and the direction of both limiting approaches. Taylor expansion yields the cubic coefficient 1/(6sqrt(2π)) for Dirichlet and slope sqrt(2/π) for Neumann, hence the quoted ratio. Independent direct kernel quadrature at c=t=0.7 gives Neumann 0.26939730485051155 and Dirichlet 0.019655636392878425, agreeing with closed forms to about 7e−17. Independent evaluation of the peak equation gives c≈0.7990017881788918 and F_+≈0.2719729564300915. These are finite cross-checks; the derivative proof, not the grid, proves global uniqueness. The original verification file and checker were inspected, not executed.
